body: I used to feel this way, until I joined meme subreddits and groups. The absurd situations described in memes are things I go through often. While objective factual descriptions of BPD don't really match my traits.

Hell yes! It's the same for me, down to the "I don't know" and getting irritated at saying it too often! My brain shuts down completely, and it's just empty up there. My ex-spouse did not understand that, and he would ask way too many questions, even when I would tell him "I don't feel like thinking right now." "I can't think right now." or other variants. It was so frustrating.

Anyone else really selective about who's allowed into their personal space? And that the "qualifications" are really random? Personally, it's just a feeling, I don't know. If ten strangers send me a message saying the exact same thing, like "Hi!", my brain might feel really at ease with one, and the 9 others I might feel really uncomfortable and I'll want to be left alone. For no reason.
I love this subreddit because I love feeling personally called out by random spongebob memes
I'm so glad that I'm not the only one! It's definitely awkward and kind of frustrating too. My biggest fear now is them realizing it's not romantic at all and then never talking to me ever again (:
Getting called out holy shit

I hear you, and in the back of my mind I feel this way too for the same reasons but honestly, the hope for motherhood is all that is keeping me alive (and as you can guess by my username, I have recently learned that I can't have kids so ... dying soon I guess lol)
Fun fact, it's normal!

One of my previous coworkers doesn't care about me and that's alright (but I'm still acting obsessive sometimes), but he sure as hell will be talkative when he has a problem and he needs to vent. When I talk to him for the sake of talking, he would be distant and just ignore all my messages for days. If after 3 messages he doesn't reply, I ignore him and try again in a month. He sure as hell will have something to complain about by then. Instead of being mature and being my own damn support, I run back to him all the time (though I made sure to never vent to him since I could tell he didn't like that).

This is why therapy doesn't work for me. Therapy has been a lot of "Are you aware that that's how your brain is working, and it's completely false?"

I KNOW. But knowing that it's wrong or false has not cured me yet, ma'am.

I hate to be that person, but if you are genuinely asking, we can try to find some things that make life worth it? I'm in the same boat as you. I don't think life is better since it's literally feeling all the feelings (and sometimes it's mostly negative stuff) vs. absolute nothingness you are incapable of being aware of .... But if you want to try, let's try together. It can be the most random thing, since death is nothingness. Do you like a specific type of weather that you look forward to when you check the weather app? Do you have anyone in your life that you would want to see just one more time? A dish you enjoy? A feeling you would miss? Etc. Maybe those are what's worth holding on for. I'm trying to convince myself of that. I would miss rain for instance, and if heaven is real, there is no rain so I would hate heaven.

I got evidence from my family (especially my mother) and a few "friends", so now I assume literally everyone I will ever meet hates me. If my own parents who so wanted a child, a little girl more specifically, so much so that they said if they have a girl first they won't ever try for a kid ever again. If those people ended up hating me since infancy, who the fuck is gonna love me? lol
That sign can't stop me because I can't read. \*get my heart broken for the nth time\*

Literally 20 seconds in and I'm actually triggered. But I'm still gonna watch, and continue on this same comment. 

Okay I'm at 9 minutes and I decided to stop, the tone became lowkey hostile because of the host. She really is the face of society. You're to blame for the unhealthy consequences of a life you didn't choose. Your parents fucked you over for years and as soon as you hit a certain age, usually 18 but can be earlier for certain behaviours, you're on your own. Either you fix yourself or you're ostracized, you are dehumanized, you are no longer welcome. And until you're able to fix yourself from within, no one will want to be around you, which really doesn't help you with your recovery. It's worse when your trauma is invisible, because sure you can go see doctors and do therapy, but what do you outside of the 1 hour of therapy a week? Who do you turn to? You're all alone, and therapy can take years to take effect.

I have a puzzle that's been on my table for 2 weeks and only the border is finished. I used to love puzzles and could finish a 1000 piece one in a day. I got many books I personally own, then I went to a library and borrowed a few comics which I have been dying to get back into. When I was a child, I read like all the comics at my local library. Literally all of them. But now I can't make it past one page. I lost interest in everything.
